avis.titre: Great product, but irriate my eyes.
avis.texte: I've been really impressed with the Medicube No Cast Just Glow Collagen Sunscreen. One of the biggest reasons I purchased it was because I wanted a sunscreen that wouldn't leave a white or ashy cast on my skin, and it definitely delivers. The formula blends in beautifully, absorbs quickly, and leaves my skin with a healthy glow rather than a greasy finish. Another huge plus is that it doesn't pill. I use it as the 7th or 8th step in my morning skincare routine, layered over multiple products, and it still applies smoothly without balling up or creating texture on the skin. It sits well under makeup and feels lightweight and comfortable throughout the day. My only complaint is that it tends to irritate my eyes. If the product migrates too close to my eye area, I experience burning and stinging. I've found myself frequently using La Roche-Posay Micellar Water on a cotton pad to remove any sunscreen residue around my eyes for relief. Overall, this is one of the better sunscreens I've tried for deeper skin tones because it leaves no white cast, layers well with skincare, and provides a beautiful glow. avis.titre: Really no white cast and actually beneficial to your skin!
avis.texte: Finding a good sunscreen can be really difficult. They’re either too heavy, too greasy, not hydrating enough, or they leave that awful white cast on your skin. I already use a few Medicube skincare products that actually delivered great results for me, so when I saw this sunscreen, one that claims to be beneficial and completely cast-free, I had to try it. And I’m so glad that I did. I immediately fell in love with this sunscreen. The formula is thin and lightweight, but not watery or runny. It has just enough thickness to feel like a proper sunscreen while still blending into the skin beautifully. It absorbs fast and doesn’t leave any white cast, like AT ALL. Instead, it gives your skin this soft, sheer glow and makes it feel smooth. It does have a traditional sunscreen smell, but it’s very subtle, which I actually appreciated because it isn’t overpowering like some SPFs can be. The formula itself is fantastic. The UV filters are all FDA-approved, and the inactive ingredients are full of skin loving benefits like hydration, brightening, soothing, anti-aging support, barrier repair, and plumping. It even contains ingredients that give a soft blurring effect and help the sunscreen apply with a smooth slip, which keeps it from pilling. I wore it under makeup, and it performed beautifully. Since it’s lightweight, it doesn’t feel heavy or sticky underneath foundation. It blurred my skin slightly and created a really nice base that didn’t cause any separation, lifting, or pilling.

Does it work or not? I don’t know, but I think so. At the very least, it does not leave a cast and It’s definitely dark skin friendly. I put it on after I do my morning routine but only in the summer or on days where I will be out working in my front yard gardening or just in the sun for a long period of time. My melanin keeps me safe from UV rays most days but being in direct sun for an extended time Period can be harmful after a while so it’s good to utilize sunscreen when needed.

What a great idea to have a sunscreen with collagen, cica, hyaluronic acid… and it works! I do find that some spf 50s have a bit of a white cast, but none of that here. avis.titre: I will be using this almost every day
avis.texte: This is an excellent daily-wear sunscreen with a lovely texture that feels balanced and comfortable. It has more body than those watery, almost serum-style SPFs on the market, which makes it both smooth and substantial. It works into the skin rather than just absorbing on its own, leaving a finish that is on the satin side of dewy. It glows but doesn’t gleam, and the result looks healthy rather than shiny. The sunscreen filters are the familiar U.S.-approved combination of homosalate, octocrylene, octisalate, and avobenzone. Together they provide proper SPF 50 broad-spectrum protection. There is no cast at all. The glide is clean, non-sticky, and very comfortable for use on the face, neck, and arms. The formula includes a range of skincare extras like niacinamide, centella components, hyaluronic acid, ceramide NP, collagen, and a peptide. These are present but at low concentrations, and while they don’t act like full skincare treatments, they do round out the feel of the formula and help with surface hydration. What stands out more is the overall texture. It's silicone-based, smooth, lightly hydrating, and easy to wear every day. There are no mismatches between the listing and the product in hand. The claims are perhaps slightly embellished in the way many SPF listings are, but everything mentioned is actually in the formula, and the product performs exactly as described regarding texture, finish, and wear. avis.titre: Of course there's no cast - it's a chemical sunscreen
avis.texte: I grabbed this because the name promised “no cast,” and technically it delivers, it’s a chemical sunscreen, so the usual white cast from mineral filters is largely avoided anyway in this. But that’s where the expectations diverged. On my mature, combination skin the finish was super glowy, almost greasy, and that’s just not what I’m comfortable with. There are definitely some great skincare ingredients in the mix like centella asiatica for soothing, squalane for moisturization, and acetyl hexapeptide-8 - a peptide that helps reduce fine lines. If your sunscreen doubles as your moisturizer (mine does) then those are great additions to this. If I weren’t used to the ultra-light, elegant formulas of Korean sunscreens (the ones with chemical filters that aren’t yet approved in the US) I might have actually liked this. As things stand, though, the texture feels too heavy and dewy for my skin type. This has a faint pink tone when dispensed, but it does not translate into any kind of tone up effect. There is a slight sunscreen-y scent to this, but it's not overwhelming, could just catch a whiff of it occasionally as I wore it. This is not a water resistant sunscreen, so please be mindful if you plan to wear this while sweating or swimming. I did not experience any eye stinging or skin irritation with this. If you’re on the hunt for a richer, glowier sunscreen and don’t mind a dewy finish, this could be worth checking out. For me though, it missed the mark.

avis.titre: I feel more shiny than glow-y
avis.texte: Alright, so I take issue with what some skincare products allege is a "glow," when I feel like on me it just looks like I'm oily or sweaty. I do think it's possible to have a slight level of shine without looking like I just worked out, but I don't know that this sunscreen succeeds on that front. There is no cast, as advertised, but the glow isn't what I'd personally call a glow so much as a shine. I would want to wear some sort of mattifying primer or similar over this if I were going to wear it out. I do like that it's made in Korea because they have high standards for cosmetics manufacturing and ingredients, but the FDA prohibits some of the best SPF ingredients from being imported into the United States, so we often get inferior versions of Korean sunscreens here.
